A_target.statement:
Let $f: \R \to \R$ be [[Definition:Twice Differentiable Real Function|twice differentiable]] with $\size {f''} \le M$.
Then:
:$\map {f'} x = \displaystyle \lim_{h \mathop \to 0} \frac {\map f {x + h} - \map f x} h$
and:
:$\size {\dfrac {\map f {x + h} - \map f x} h - \map {f'} x} \le \dfrac {M h} 2$

B_source.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a [[Definition:Real Sequence|real sequence]].
The [[Definition:Forward Difference|forward difference]] of $\sequence {a_n}$ is:
:$\paren {\Delta a}_n = a_{n + 1} - a_n$

validity_conditions: f must be twice differentiable for the error term to be O(h)
the step size must tend to zero for the discrete operator to converge to the continuous one
proof_plan: Sample $f$ on the grid $x + h \Z$ and form the [[Definition:Forward Difference|forward differences]] $\map f {x + h} - \map f x$.

By [[Taylor's Theorem]] with [[Definition:Lagrange Form of Remainder|Lagrange remainder]]:
:$\map f {x + h} = \map f x + h \map {f'} x + \dfrac {h^2} 2 \map {f''} \xi$
for some $\xi$ between $x$ and $x + h$.

Dividing by $h$:
:$\dfrac {\map f {x + h} - \map f x} h - \map {f'} x = \dfrac h 2 \map {f''} \xi$
whose absolute value is at most $\dfrac {M h} 2$.
Letting $h \to 0$, the difference quotient converges to $\map {f'} x$.
